hints: Both particles fall with the same g, so relative to each other they move in straight lines at constant velocity. For B to be hit, which way must A’s velocity relative to B point?
worded:
1. Both have acceleration g, so their relative motion is uniform and straight.

2. They start on the same level, a distance x apart. To meet, A’s velocity relative to B must point along AB, i.e. horizontally. So the vertical components must be equal: 20 sin θ = 10, θ = 30°.

3. The relative velocity is then purely horizontal: 20 cos 30° − 0 = 10√3 m/s.

4. In 0.5 s it closes x = 10√3 × 0.5 = 5√3 m. (D)
conventional:
![](asset:P000248-sol-1)

Collision condition (equal vertical components): $20\sin\theta = 10 \Rightarrow \theta = 30^{\circ}$.

$$v_{AB} = 20\cos 30^{\circ} = 10\sqrt{3}\unit{m/s},\quad\quad x = v_{AB}\, t = 10\sqrt{3} \times 0.5 = 5\sqrt{3}\unit{m}.$$
mistakes: Gravity drops out of the relative motion; do not add ½gt² to either particle when comparing them.
(A) 10√3 is the relative speed, not the distance covered in 0.5 s.
